paper_id: Exploring LLM-based Data Annotation Strategies for Medical Dialogue Preference Alignment
title: Exploring LLM-based Data Annotation Strategies for Medical Dialogue Preference Alignment
motivation: Preference-aligned data annotation in medical dialogue requires expensive expert involvement; current automated evaluation methods are unreliable and LLM preferences deviate from physician preferences.
problem_framing: Define the unlabeled preference dataset D = <H, C1, F1, C2, F2> and find effective annotation function f: D → D' for training medical dialogue models using DPO.
key_insight: Physicians' preferences can be depicted using flowcharts that represent diagnostic decision logic, which can then be converted into rules for preference data annotation.
method_signature: Multi-agent annotation with Planner (long-term goal setting), Ranker (response evaluation), and Rethinker (response generation) to replace expert involvement.
evaluation_criteria: Standardized patient testing (CSPT) for user guidance; WebMedQA for instruction following; hybrid multi-round evaluation combining both competencies.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Training with Rethinker-generated data alone compromises instruction-following ability due to overfitting to guidance-dominant responses.
evidence_for_taste: GPT-4 preferences deviate from human physicians
